heading: Modelling built on first-principle physics, run at production scale.
lead: Every model we deliver traces back to the governing equations of multiphase, multicomponent flow in porous and fractured rock — not a black box. We calibrate against field observations, then push the model through HPC-scale ensembles to quantify what we don't yet know.

capabilities.title: Numerical reservoir modelling
capabilities.description: Finite-volume, integral-finite-difference simulation of non-isothermal multiphase flow — natural-state calibration through decades-long production forecasting, in both single-porosity and fractured dual-porosity formulations.

capabilities.title: Parallel computing
capabilities.description: Production and exploration models are run as MPI-parallel ensembles on NeSI HPC clusters, turning multi-day single runs into same-day scenario comparisons.

capabilities.title: Uncertainty quantification
capabilities.description: Permeability, porosity and boundary conditions are treated as distributions, not point estimates — ensemble and history-matching methods translate geological uncertainty into a defensible resource-risk range.

capabilities.title: Software & tools
capabilities.description: TOUGH3 and Waiwera for the core physics, extended with proprietary Python and Julia tooling for mesh generation, automated calibration, and post-processing.

methodology.heading: Two methods from our in-preparation resource assessment paper
methodology.lead: Drawn directly from our Tecuamburro–Infiernitos combined resource assessment manuscript (in preparation, not yet peer-reviewed) — the automated well-siting logic and pump-sizing safety margin behind the case study below.

items.title: Automated well-siting: the growth algorithm
items.description: Production wells are added one at a time: every candidate block is scored on deliverability, the best is added as a well, its immediate neighbours are removed from the candidate list, and the reservoir simulation is re-run from that new state before the next candidate is scored — repeating until the additional steam gained drops below threshold. Reinjection wells grow the same way in parallel, ranked by permeability and drawdown, until reinjection pressure would exceed a defined limit. Every candidate is re-scored against the model's own updated state at each step, not a static initial guess.

items.title: Two-tier pump sizing under gas-breakout pressure (GBOP)
items.description: For CO2-bearing geothermal fluid, dissolved gas comes out of solution before the fluid reaches its own boiling point — a water-only NPSH threshold under-protects the pump. We size to GBOP (saturation pressure plus the fluid's own NCG partial pressure) plus a fixed safety margin, evaluated automatically for every candidate well at every growth step, then matched against a real vendor pump catalogue — line-shaft or electric submersible, up to 30 stages — for a buildable specification and its parasitic shaft power.
